title: Kernel circuit breaker and replay-safe degradation for multi-stream CUDA graph decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Multi-stream decode uses CUDA graph capture/replay for prefill+decode. In high-throughput environments we have observed intermittent replay failures caused by kernel mismatches (e.g., different kernel heuristics triggered between capture and replay) and rare races when a captured graph contains a kernel that is later evicted/quantized differently. Goal: introduce a runtime circuit breaker and controlled degradation path that detects kernel incompatibility at replay time, safely falls back to a non-graph decode path (or an alternate compatible kernel set), and emits detailed telemetry for postmortem and automated remediation. This reduces P99 failures and provides safer rollout of new kernel-selection logic and quantization profiles.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime detects kernel signature mismatch on replay and triggers deterministic fallback within 2 ms of detection
2) Fallback paths: (a) replay with alternate kernel set, or (b) switch to streaming decode without CUDA graphs. Both must preserve correctness and not leak KV-cache state between streams

3) Telemetry emitted for every circuit-breaker event: trace_id, model, kernel_signature_at_capture, kernel_signature_at_replay, active_quant_profile, device_id, available_memory, stack_snapshot, and chosen fallback
4) Unit and integration tests cover simulated kernel-race and quantization-change scenarios with deterministic assertions
5) End-to-end perf regressions at P50/P90 remain within configured SLOs for conservative fallback policy (default: prefer alternate kernel set before full streaming fallback)
6) Feature gated with runtime flag and annotated in rollout dashboard
7) Documentation updated (Console runbook + DEV runbook) with recovery steps and safe rollout guidance
implementation_steps: 1. Instrument kernel selection module to produce compact kernel_signature (hash of kernel attributes and compilation flags) and persist it in graph metadata during capture
2. Add a lightweight kernel_signature verifier executed at replay start; if mismatch, classify failure (minor: compatible, major: incompatible)
3. Implement circuit-breaker state machine: CLOSED -> OPEN (on X failures in window) -> HALF_OPEN (trial replays) with exponential backoff and pluggable policy
4. Build two fallback strategies: (A) alternate-kernel lookup and graph-rewrite path, (B) streaming decode path that executes without CUDA graphs but reuses KV cache snapshots
5. Emit structured events to telemetry backend (trace + metric + log) and add dashboard panels in Console for circuit-breaker metrics
6. Add integration tests in runner that fuzzes kernel selection changes between capture/replay and asserts correctness under fallback
7. Create canary rollout plan with traffic split, observability thresholds, and automatic rollback criteria
8. Document runtime flag and operator runbook; add a small CLI to force-reset circuit breaker for a device or model
updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting with serving runtime and infra teams. Agreed to use 3-field kernel_signature (arch, config_hash, compile_flags_hash) to balance size and uniqueness.

2026-02-25: Spike: implemented prototype verifier and reproduced an internal flaky replay by toggling quant_profile at runtime. Collected signature diffs. PR: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/9876 (WIP).
2026-02-28: Design review with PM (Marta Lopez) and SRE. Discussed two fallback modes; decided to prefer alternate-kernel rewrite first to avoid latency cliff for high-SLA customers.
2026-03-03: Telemetry schema finalized (trace fields + tags). Instrumentation added to capture path. Draft dashboard created: https://console.redwood.team/d/dec-rel/circuit-breaker-view

2026-03-06: Integration test harness added to repo runner to simulate kernel eviction events. Found KV cache snapshot edge-case: when falling back to streaming decode we must rehydrate per-stream KV state; added explicit KV snapshot/restore API. PR: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/9921

2026-03-09: Performance smoke: alternate-kernel rewrite adds median +0.8ms, streaming fallback adds +5-7ms P90. We need to tune default policy: prefer rewrite unless memory pressure > 70% then stream. Recorded baseline dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/dec-rel/baseline
2026-03-10: Security review requested (KMS/metadata exposure checks). Filed sec ticket SEC-214 and blocked on keys access clarification.
Next steps: finish PRs, add canary orchestration (cycle 2026-W10), and run a week-long canary on low-traffic models.
